Supabase is the open-source Postgres development platform that 7M+ developers and thousands of enterprises depend on every day. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

We’re looking for a Product Manager, Marketplace to join our Product Team to lead our marketplace and integration surfaces.
The marketplace is the two-sided surface of the Supabase ecosystem. On one side, Partners and developers build integrations on top of Supabase primitives like Auth, Storage, and Edge Functions, then publish them for the world to use. On the other, our developers come to discover new capabilities and wire them into their projects without leaving their workflow. Done well, it is the shortest path between a developer with a problem and the exact capability that solves it.
That surface is about to matter more than ever. As the number of capabilities explodes, and as agents begin to assemble software on a developer's behalf, the marketplace becomes the distribution and discovery layer for the whole ecosystem: how both developers and, increasingly, their agents find, trust, and compose what they need. This role owns it.

Own the product strategy and roadmap for the marketplace, the two-sided surface where Partners and developers publish integrations and where Supabase's developer customers discover and install them.
Make it effortless for a developer to find the right capability and integrate it. Own discovery, search, listings, and the whole path from install to working integration, so a new capability connects to Supabase primitives and runs inside a developer's project with minimal glue code.
Make publishing an integration fast and rewarding, so Partners and developers bring their best work to the marketplace and keep it current, and so the catalog stays deep where developers need it.
Set the quality bar and the listing standards, and build the review, guardrail, and versioning mechanisms, with Engineering and our Partnerships team, that keep the catalog trustworthy as it scales.
Own what a healthy marketplace looks like: define the metrics across both supply and demand, instrument the surface end to end, and let the signal rather than opinion drive what gets built next.
Position the marketplace as the distribution layer for agent-driven development, where capabilities get discovered and composed on a builder's behalf rather than browsed and installed by hand.

s.h: You might be a good fit if you
s.t:
Have 7+ years of product management on developer tools or marketplaces , or are an ex-founder with strong product instincts, and can identify which partners and integrations will matter most, with particular instinct for the agentic and code-first integrations now defining how developers build.
Have built and grown a two-sided surface: an app store, a plugin or integration ecosystem, a developer platform, or a marketplace, and understand the chicken-and-egg of balancing supply and demand, recruiting developers, driving listing quality, and making discovery and install effortless for the consuming side. Experience with app stores or developer-platform distribution is a strong plus.
Are biased toward speed , and would rather ship something imperfect and learn than spend another sprint polishing a spec.
Build with what you own, using the marketplace from both sides: publishing a test integration the way a Partner would, and sourcing and wiring one into a project the way a developer would. You form opinions through first-hand use.
Use AI tools to compress the slow parts of the job, like research, drafting, and synthesising feedback, so you spend more time on judgment calls.
Work async by default. Supabase is fully remote, so you make decisions in writing and move work forward without meetings.

Fully Remote
We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.
Tech Allowance
Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.
Annual Off-Sites
Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.
Flexible Work
We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.
Professional Development
Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

Who We Are We started our company to help others launch and run their own businesses, at any stage. The way we help is by keeping it simple and supporting entrepreneurs one step at a time. Put simply: our mission is to enable anyone to start, run, and grow their business while avoiding the common pitfalls that derail hopeful entrepreneurs.

No more having to wade through forms, taxes, or ongoing state compliance. We are a remote company based in Austin, Texas. We have team members from Florida to Oregon and all points in-between. Take pride in your work knowing that it shapes how people all across the country reach their goal of starting, running, and growing their business.

If the idea of helping people and working with a genuinely caring, supportive team excites you, then you’ve come to the right place. The Role We're hiring a Staff Product Manager to own the logged-in customer experience at ZenBusiness — the first experience a new business owner sees after signing up and starting to run their company.

This role is about everything that happens after completing their formation: how we keep them coming back, deepening the value they get from our product suite, and turning first-time customers into long-term relationships. You'll own the product roadmap for our native apps (iOS and Android) and web dashboard.

Your mandate is to create a unified, delightful, self-serve experience that helps business owners get more out of every ZenBusiness product they own — from formations and compliance to marketing and fintech — and to drive more awareness and attachment of our highest-value offerings they don’t yet own.

This is a high-visibility individual contributor role that reports directly to the VP of Product, Growth. Responsibilities Build a unified product experience with Velo at the center Define and drive the product roadmap for the logged-in Web & native app experiences, focused on engagement depth, repeat usage, and in-app monetization.

Partner with our Velo team to bring our AI business guide to the center of our logged in experience, leveraging the unique capabilities of our agentic platform to do more for our business owners.

Collaborate closely with the product managers who own our individual products — formations, compliance, marketing, and fintech — to bring the best of each into a single, coherent customer experience. Identify and run experiments to lift core engagement, retention, and product-attachment metrics.

Work cross-functionally with design, engineering, and marketing to execute against that vision. Drive usage and attachment of our highest-value products Drive activation across our product suite by directly leading activation initiatives and equipping other PMs with the tools to drive activation themselves.

If a customer paid for it, your job is to get them to use it. Drive higher activation and usage of our key formations, compliance, marketing, and fintech products by surfacing the right capability at the right moment.

Increase awareness and attachment of our highest-value products through thoughtful CTAs, cross-sell sequencing, and upsell entry points — without compromising the customer experience. Use experimentation and customer data to find friction in the purchase funnel and optimize conversion at every step.

Act as the primary Product point of contact across product marketing, customer success, finance, and other teams that contribute to increasing customer attach rate and retention.

Operate as a builder Use AI across the product lifecycle — research, ideation, prototyping, experiment design — with tools like Claude, Lovable, v0, and Replit as your default mode of working, not a one-off. Prototype your high-potential ideas and put them in front of real customers or internal users for rapid feedback and iteration.

Contribute to our product features that create real customer value — with the judgment to know where AI deepens the experience vs. where it's a distraction. What We're Looking For 6+ years of product management experience, with at least 2 years at a Staff or senior PM level.

Proven track record owning mobile app products (iOS and/or Android) — you understand the platform, the patterns, and how to drive engagement on native surfaces. Demonstrated ability to design unified experiences across multiple products and partner closely with other PMs to make the whole greater than the sum of its parts.

Experience designing self-serve customer experiences with thoughtful escalation paths to human support. Strong instincts around monetization — you know how to position products, write CTAs, structure purchase flows, and find the friction that kills conversion.

Experience working across web and native apps simultaneously; you think in customer journeys, not platforms. Strong collaborator with design and engineering; you can drive decisions without authority. Comfortable in ambiguity — this role requires you to set direction, not execute someone else's roadmap.

Bonus: experience with AI-powered product features, SMB or subscription products, or growth experimentation. Why This Role Matters ZenBusiness serves over 1 million small business owners, and our product suite spans formations, compliance, marketing, and fintech.

This role exists to ensure that entrepreneurs can use ZenBusiness as their operating system to confidently grow their business. The dashboard and native app are where the ZenBusiness experience comes to life. Remote Culture. A great company culture leads to happy employees, and happy employees lead to happy customers.

We provide our employees with good salaries, benefits, equity, and interesting challenges that have a positive impact. Let’s stay connected! We believe in staying connected, and we have a weekly “All Hands” meeting every week. We also have a social committee that hosts frequent events.

We’ve held a virtual talent show, costume competitions, monthly lunch and learn series, Hackathons and more! Benefits. The company offers various benefits to employees and their dependents, including medical, vision, dental, disability, and life insurance, as well as parental and military leave.

Other benefits include an employee assistance program, 401k + match, annual bonus, pet insurance, and RSUs. Paid parking* and 10 paid holidays are also provided. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion. We believe in diversity, equity & inclusion .

At ZenBusiness , every voice counts no matter your race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, age, location, or background. We celebrate the diversity of our teams, knowing that our products, services, and customers thrive best when we lean into and celebrate our differences.

Please check out our careers' page to learn more about our culture, benefits, and open opportunities. *applicable to in-office employees Originally posted on Himalayas

About the role Automated video editing is an emerging category, and we're positioned to define it. Media companies want to turn thousands of podcast episodes into social clips. Marketing teams want to automatically create product demos for every release. Agencies want to process client content in bulk with consistent branding.

And they want to do all of that at scale. As the Product Manager for this 0 to 1 area, you'll build and own the platform that makes this all possible. You'll create APIs that let developers programmatically import media, run AI-powered edits, and export content.

StackAdapt is the leading technology company that empowers marketers to reach, engage, and convert audiences with precision. The most forward-thinking marketers choose StackAdapt to orchestrate high-impact campaigns across programmatic advertising and marketing channels.
The Creatives team is on a mission to build a one-stop-shop for advertisers' creative production and management needs.

We're developing a comprehensive in-house product that lets clients create, enhance, preview, store, and manage CTV, video, audio, DOOH, display, and native ads at scale — whether they start from ready-made templates or build from scratch.

By delivering a robust, full-featured in-house solution, we reduce our clients' reliance on costly third-party creative providers and empower advertisers to move faster and more efficiently.
The next chapter for the team centers on AI-powered content generation and a multi-channel creative experience, with particular focus on AI first video and CTV solutions. It's a high-impact, fast-moving area with significant room to define the product, the technology, and the creative workflows that will set the standard for how advertisers build at scale.
As a Senior Product Manager on the Creatives team, you'll own a portfolio at the heart of this ambition. This is a 0→1 space that spans multiple teams and disciplines, and you'll set the direction for it: shaping strategy, making the hard calls, and shipping. You'll partner closely with Engineering, Design, Creative Studio, Data Science, and Revenue to translate a bold vision into products advertisers love.
StackAdapt is a remote first company. This role is open to candidates in Canada and the United States.
What You'll Be Doing
Own the strategy, roadmap, and end-to-end delivery for a portfolio spanning the video/CTV creative builder, AI-generated and brand content products, and creative integrations with social and partner platforms.
Lead 0→1 initiatives from first principles — research and validate the problem, frame the opportunity, define the path forward, and drive it to launch and adoption.
Translate complex, cross-team problems into a clear vision and crisp, actionable requirements that give Engineering, Design, and QE unambiguous direction on how features should behave.
Partner with Data Science and Engineering to shape how AI/ML and generative content capabilities are applied across creative formats, making sound technical trade-offs along the way.
Define key success metrics, monitor KPIs, and make data-informed decisions about what to build, what to cut, and what to double down on.
Work hand-in-hand with Creative Studio to ensure the tooling reflects real creative workflows and produces work that meets a high creative and brand bar.
Build new integrations with external platforms, partnering across teams to open up a wider range of creative assets and ad formats within the creative library.
Communicate precisely and proactively across the organization, keeping stakeholders aligned and informed at the right level and the right time.
Support customer-facing teams by resolving questions about your portfolio and helping triage bugs and regressions as they appear.

s.h: What You'll Bring to the Table
s.t:
Proven experience as a Product Manager at a technology company, with a track record of shipping large, complex software products end-to-end (and you can speak to your successes).
Demonstrated success leading 0→1 initiatives that span multiple teams — you bring structure and direction to new problem spaces and rally others around a clear plan.
Experience building products in AdTech, MarTech, or creative platforms, with a meaningful edge for those who've worked on creative-building or generative AI products.
Strong fluency with AI/ML and generative AI concepts — enough to partner deeply with Data Science and Engineering, reason about capabilities and limitations, and make informed product decisions.
A technical background (Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent hands-on experience) that lets you discuss technical trade-offs, integrations, and architecture credibly with engineers.
A keen design and creative sense, balanced with technical depth — you pair an eye for what "great" looks like with the ability to partner closely with engineering on how to build it.
An excellent cross-functional collaborator who can tailor your approach across Engineering, Design, Creative Studio, Data Science, and Revenue without skipping a beat.
Clear, structured writing and communication — you distill complex ideas into words that build consensus and align stakeholders around your vision.
Strong prioritization instincts grounded in reason, clarity, and purpose — you focus the team on the most impactful work and the KPIs you're moving.
A leadership style rooted in influence rather than formal authority, and the judgment to operate independently in a fast-moving, evolving space.

At Mural, we're changing how teams collaborate, think, and make decisions together. The Growth & Engagement team owns the experiences that turn a single-player tool into a multiplayer habit: the loops that bring people back, help them find their work, and pull their colleagues into a mural. Mural's self-serve growth runs through these experiences, and engagement and retention are central to how the business grows.

As Senior Product Manager, Growth & Engagement, you will own the end-to-end self-serve experience, from a user's first touch through activation, return usage, and conversion to paid. You will treat the full funnel as one system: acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, sharing, and monetization.

You will run a high-tempo experimentation practice, partner deeply across Product, Engineering, Design, Data, Marketing, and Sales, and make the calls that turn occasional users into teams that rely on Mural every week. This is a role for someone who wants to own real growth outcomes, not just ship features.
You will own the surfaces that decide whether Mural's self-serve engine grows. Seamless integration and expansion of new local payment methods and features into the core PPRO platform, replacing legacy integration methods.

You know version control is more than just a subsystem. It’s the backbone of how teams build software. You’re ready to shape the future of code-change workflows, from local commits to AI-assisted reviews. If you’re excited by the challenge of turning a core IDE feature into a standalone ecosystem, this is for you.
About JetBrains
We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.

Version control is a critical part of our IDEs, but we want to take it further. We’re turning VCS into a strategic product direction and, eventually, we aim to grow it into a dedicated ecosystem. This role exists to define what that future looks like right now.
As the Senior Product Manager, you’ll figure out where JetBrains should play in the VCS space, how to evolve our Git and code review experiences, and what new opportunities exist beyond our current tools.

You’ll have the ownership to set a clear product vision that covers everything from complex local merges to remote, containerized, and AI-assisted workflows. You’ll collaborate closely with engineering and quality leads, as well as product marketing, developer advocacy, and the IntelliJ Platform teams.

Together, you'll figure out how to handle the next era of software delivery, including tracking provenance and reviewing AI-generated changes across different environments.

Set the long-term product strategy for VCS and code-change workflows across all JetBrains IDEs.
Identify gaps in current developer workflows and define new product directions in the VCS space.
Explore new opportunities, from cross-IDE VCS clients and host-neutral code reviews to AI-native review and authorship tracking.
Listen closely to what the community and the industry are saying to figure out exactly what we should be working on.
Align roadmap decisions across the product, engineering, design, marketing, developer advocacy, partnership, and customer-facing teams.
Work with engineering and quality leads to balance user value, technical constraints, and platform health.
Shape external positioning and represent our VCS direction in conversations with customers and the broader developer tools community.

A collaborative mindset that works well with engineering and quality teams on deeply technical challenges.
Strong product judgment, especially when navigating ambiguous areas to define a new ecosystem.
The ability to think beyond existing boundaries and spot opportunities for entirely new workflows.
Clear communication skills, whether you’re aligning internal stakeholders or talking to deeply technical users.
A data-informed approach, combining usage metrics, customer feedback, and market signals to make decisions.
An interest in how AI is changing software development, from generated commits to AI-assisted reviews.
A drive to improve solutions instead of copying what already exists.
What you’ll need
Previous success leading the product direction and strategy for technically complex developer tools, SCM, CI/CD, or code collaboration software.
The proven ability to translate intricate developer workflows into clear product roadmaps.
Experience bringing stakeholders together across product, engineering, marketing, and developer advocacy.
A deep understanding of version control mechanics, code-change workflows, and how developers actually ship code.
Based in the EU, ideally Munich, Prague, Amsterdam, Berlin, Belgrade, or remote within the EU, with the ability to travel to JetBrains offices as needed.
As a plus, familiarity with advanced version control scenarios, such as complex merges, monorepos, and enterprise/self-hosted setups.
What success looks like
Success means moving VCS from a platform subsystem to a clear, strategic ecosystem. You’ll have built a compelling product vision that engineering teams are aligned on and customers are excited about. You won’t just be copying what exists.

You’ll be finding entirely new ways to solve code-change workflows, especially as AI becomes a bigger part of development. Ultimately, you’ll earn your team's trust by making sound decisions, keeping projects moving, and leaving the product better than you found it.

· Comfortable leading customer discovery and validation conversations and turning qualitative and quantitative insights into product decisions.

· Proven ability to influence and align cross ‑ functional partners and senior stakeholders without formal authority.

· Data ‑ driven mindset: confident with metrics, experimentation and basic quantitative reasoning to set goals, measure impact and debug product issues.

· Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas simply to both technical and non ‑ technical audiences.

Die campoint AG ist Technologiepartner und Betreiber einer der größten deutschsprachigen Plattformen für die Creator Economy und Digital Entertainment - von der Consumer-Plattform bis zur B2B-Infrastruktur, mit der Creators und Agenturen ihr Business aufbauen und steuern.

Dabei sind Creators für uns keine User, sondern Unternehmer, deren Erfolg unmittelbar von unseren Produkten abhängt. Das bestimmt, wie wir priorisieren. Wir gestalten nach unserer Vision. Wir leben von Teamplay, Hands-on-Mentalität und einer Kommunikation auf Augenhöhe.
Aufgaben
Du bekommst echte Ownership für zugewiesene Produkt-Streams innerhalb unseres B2B-Portfolios. Das bedeutet: Du entscheidest, was gebaut wird und was nicht - auf Basis von Creator-Feedback, Umsatzdaten und strategischem Rahmen. Wir haben keine langen Abstimmungsrunden. Du bist das Quality-Gateway für Dein Team und Eure Releases.
Du navigierst eigenständig durch ein komplexes Stakeholder-Umfeld. Wir erwarten, dass Du Konflikte direkt löst - nicht eskalierst.
Die strategische Richtung gibt der Head of Product vor. Deine Aufgabe ist es, sie mit hoher Eigenständigkeit und Qualitätsanspruch umzusetzen und innerhalb Deiner Streams bessere Entscheidungen zu treffen, als wenn er sie selbst treffen würde.
Das ist kein Stepping-Stone in die Produktstrategie. Das ist eine Rolle für jemanden, der im Operativen exzellent ist und das als Stärke sieht, nicht als Einschränkung.
Du verantwortest Discovery, Priorisierung und Delivery in Deinen Produkt-Streams von Anfang bis Ende.
Du übersetzt qualitative Creator-Insights und starke Signale direkt in mutige Entscheidungen - ohne Dich in endlosen Datenanalysen ("Analysis Paralysis") zu verlieren.
Du schreibst klare Specs und Tickets, die ohne Nacharbeit ins Development gehen.
Du erkennst, wann ein Prozess oder Sprint-Ritual der schnellen Problemlösung im Weg steht, und brichst es pragmatisch in Absprache mit dem Team auf.
Du holst externe Impulse aktiv rein und arbeitest sie pragmatisch ein.
Du behältst den Überblick über technische Abhängigkeiten, ohne Dich in ihnen zu verlieren.
Qualifikation

Du hast 4–6 Jahre Erfahrung als PO oder PM in einem digitalen Produkt-Umfeld mit nachweisbarer Execution-Qualität, nicht nur Prozess-Compliance.
Du baust Dir schnell echtes Verständnis von Plattform-Logik, Creator-Mindset und wirtschaftlichen Zusammenhängen auf.
Du besitzt ein hohes UX-Gespür und ästhetisches Urteil: Du erkennst intuitiv gute Usability und kannst Design-Entscheidungen aus Creator-Sicht begründen, statt sie nur analytisch zu zerlegen.
Du verfügst über eine wirtschaftliche und psychologische Intuition rund um Monetarisierung, Nutzerverhalten und Einkommenspsychologie.
Deine Sprachkenntnisse: Deutsch fließend, Englisch working proficiency.

Du nutzt AI-Tools (Claude Cowork, ChatGPT o.ä.) selbstverständlich für Discovery, Spec-Writing und Priorisierung - nicht als Spielerei, sondern um schneller zu besseren Entscheidungen zu kommen.
Du bewertest AI-Output kritisch, statt ihn unreflektiert zu übernehmen - Du erkennst Halluzinationen und schwache Annahmen.
Du verstehst, wo AI in unseren Produkten selbst Creator-Mehrwert schaffen kann und denkst das aktiv in Deiner Priorisierung mit.

Du besitzt Erfahrung mit Creator-/Freelancer-Plattformen, Subscription-Flows oder Content-Monetarisierung.
Du hast bereits in einem regulatorisch komplexen Umfeld gearbeitet.
Du verfügst über Erfahrung mit Prompt-Engineering oder dem Aufbau AI-gestützter Workflows/Agenten in Deinem bisherigen PM-Alltag.

Flexibilität, die passt: Mit flexiblen Arbeitszeiten und der Option auf Remote-Arbeit gestaltest Du Deinen Arbeitstag so, wie er für Dich am besten funktioniert.
Inspiration und Freiraum: Unser moderner Campus bietet nicht nur ein kreatives Arbeitsumfeld, sondern auch einen eigenen Outdoor-Bereich mit Grill- und Volleyballplatz – der perfekte Ort, um Energie zu tanken und neue Ideen zu entwickeln.
Gemeinsam stark: Wir leben eine Kultur, die auf Wertschätzung, Vertrauen und Offenheit basiert. Flache Hierarchien und agile Strukturen sorgen dafür, dass jede Meinung zählt und wir auf Augenhöhe zusammenarbeiten.
Bereit für Deinen Start: Ab Tag eins bist Du bestens ausgestattet. Topaktuelle Hardware, persönliche Welcome Bag und ein Onboarding, das Dich wirklich abholt.
Dein Wachstum, unser Antrieb: Wir investieren in Deine Weiterbildung! Ob durch unser vielfältiges Trainingsangebot oder individuelle Fortbildungsmöglichkeiten – wir unterstützen Dich auf Deinem Weg.
Aktiv und fit: Mit JobRad zur Arbeit, Trainingseinheiten im eigenen Fitnessstudio, Beachvolleyball-Matches oder Laufgruppen – unser sportliches Angebot kennt keine Grenzen. Für Abenteuerlustige steht auch mal ein Ausflug nach Sölden auf dem Plan!
Unvergessliche Momente: Ob Sommerfeste, Weihnachtsfeiern oder spontane Team-Events - wir feiern gemeinsam die Erfolge und den Spaß an der Arbeit.
Das gewisse Extra: Bester Kaffee aus Siebträgermaschinen, frisches Bio-Obst und freie Getränke.
Klingt nach Dir?
Dann freuen wir uns auf Deine Bewerbung! Uns interessiert vor allem, was Dich antreibt, warum die Rolle zu Dir passt und wann Du bei uns starten könntest.

Ein erster Einblick: Wir, die MIFCOM GmbH, bieten die besten Jobs in der Gaming-Branche. Als einer der führenden Hersteller persönlich konfigurierbarer PCs und Notebooks für Gamer und anspruchsvolle Nutzer sind wir immer auf der Suche nach neuen Talenten, mit einem Faible für Technik, die gemeinsam mit uns ihren nächsten Karriereschritt machen wollen.
Mit über 180 engagierten Mitarbeitern fertigen wir an 2 Standorten PCs, Workstations und Server nach Kundenwunsch. Egal ob Business-Laptop oder High-End Gaming PC, wir setzen alles daran die Vorstellungen unserer Kunden umzusetzen – „Geht nicht, gibt’s nicht!“
Dabei sind ein Höchstmaß an Flexibilität, bedingungslose Kundenorientierung und eine ausgesprochene Hands-On Mentalität die Grundpfeiler unserer täglichen Arbeit. Vielfach von der Fachpresse ausgezeichnet und mit besten Kundenbewertungen sind wir der führende PC-Systembuilder in Deutschland.
Zur Verstärkung unseres Produktmanagement-Teams suchen wir aktuell einen Produktmanager – PC-Komponenten & Systemkonfiguration (m/w/d) . In dieser Rolle bringst Du ein breites Verständnis für PC-Konfigurationen und Komponentenökosysteme mit und entwickelst diesen Bereich innerhalb unseres Produktmanagements aktiv weiter. Du bist der Spezialist für das Zusammenspiel der Teile – mit einem Schwerpunkt auf Kühlung, Lüfter und Gehäuse, aber nie ohne den Blick aufs Gesamtsystem.
Deine Aufgaben: Als Produktmanager – PC-Komponenten & Systemkonfiguration (m/w/d) verantwortest Du Sortiment, Prozesse und Lieferantenbeziehungen in Deinen Warengruppen und bringst gleichzeitig Dein Systemverständnis ein, um unser Konfigurationsangebot kontinuierlich zu verbessern.
Der Schwerpunkt liegt im Produktmanagement – ergänzt um einkaufsnahe Aufgaben wie Verhandlungen und Konditionsgestaltung.
Deine täglichen To-Dos umfassen vor allem die folgenden Tätigkeiten:
Du übernimmst die Sortimentsstrategie für PC-Komponenten mit einem Schwerpunkt auf Kühler, Lüfter und Gehäuse – von der Produktauswahl und technischen Validierung über Kompatibilitätsprüfungen bis hin zur Weiterentwicklung des Gesamtportfolios
Du bringst ein ganzheitliches Verständnis für PC-Konfigurationen mit; Du denkst nicht in einzelnen Bauteilen, sondern erkennst, wie Komponenten im System zusammenwirken und nutzt dieses Wissen, um unser Konfigurationsangebot gezielt weiterzuentwickeln
Du übernimmst das Vendor Management für Deine Warengruppen und bist interner Hauptansprechpartner für Hersteller und Distributoren in allen technischen und kommerziellen Fragestellungen
Du führst Lieferantenverhandlungen zu Einkaufskonditionen, Rahmenverträgen, Rabattstaffeln und Sonderaktionen und optimierst so kontinuierlich unsere Marge und Verfügbarkeit
Du bewertest neue Produkte technisch fundiert hinsichtlich Kompatibilität, Leistung und Verarbeitungsqualität – bei Lüftern und Kühlern spielen dabei auch Design und Ästhetik eine wichtige Rolle: Formgebung, Beleuchtungskonzepte und aktuelle Optik-Trends beeinflussen die Kaufentscheidung unserer Kunden
Du behältst Markt-, Trend- und Wettbewerbsentwicklungen im Blick und leitest daraus Sortiments- und Preisentscheidungen ab
Du pflegst und verwaltest die Artikel Deiner Warengruppen inklusive technischer Detaildaten in unserem Warenwirtschaftssystem und Onlineshop
Du treibst die Weiterentwicklung unserer Produktmanagement-Prozesse aktiv voran – von Forecasting und Reporting bis zur abteilungsübergreifenden Zusammenarbeit mit Einkauf, Produktion und Service
Du stehst im engen Austausch mit anderen Teams aus den Bereichen Einkauf, Produktion und Service, um Sortiments- und Verfügbarkeitsthemen frühzeitig zu klären

Du hast ein gutes Gespür für Design und Ästhetik, insbesondere bei Lüftern und Kühlern, und erkennst, welche Optik und welches Beleuchtungskonzept bei unserer Zielgruppe ankommt

En TCIT valoramos a profesionales que puedan liderar el “puente” entre negocio y tecnología: traducir necesidades, ordenar el trabajo del equipo y sostener el foco en el resultado.
Requisitos y experiencia
Formación: Ingeniería Industrial, Informática y/o Civil.
Experiencia implementando soluciones tecnológicas y productos digitales en el sector financiero.
Dominio de metodologías ágiles para la gestión de productos y la coordinación con equipos.
Habilidades de comunicación para alinear requerimientos con heads de negocio y stakeholders.
Experiencia en empresas de Banca y/o Fintech.
Manejo de Inglés B1-B2

Orientación a resultados y capacidad para priorizar según valor de negocio.

Alta coordinación y seguimiento: sostener el backlog, la planificación y la entrega incremental.
Comunicación clara y proactiva, adaptando el lenguaje entre negocio y tecnología.
Colaboración: trabajo efectivo con proveedores, equipos de desarrollo y áreas internas.
Si te entusiasma liderar productos digitales con enfoque en calidad y sostenibilidad, y disfrutas trabajar con equipos ágiles en entornos Cloud, este desafío es para ti.
Nuestra misión es asegurar que las soluciones digitales evolucionen de forma ordenada, medible y alineada al negocio. Tu foco será convertir necesidades y oportunidades en un backlog claro y accionable, liderando la planificación y el seguimiento del producto durante todo su ciclo de vida.

Liderar el ciclo de vida de las soluciones digitales: discovery, definición, planificación, entrega y mejora continua.
Transformar iniciativas de negocio en un backlog claro, priorizado y mantenido (con criterios de valor, alcance y dependencias).
Gestionar el presupuesto del producto/solución, coordinando costos, recursos y planificación con las áreas correspondientes.
Coordinar con proveedores, equipos de desarrollo y stakeholders para asegurar ejecución efectiva y alineamiento.
Definir y hacer seguimiento de objetivos del producto, métricas y resultados esperados, para una gestión basada en datos.
Dominar metodologías ágiles (por ejemplo, Scrum/Kanban) y asegurar prácticas saludables de trabajo con los equipos.
Trabajar con tecnologías Cloud en AWS (u otras), comprendiendo el impacto de decisiones de arquitectura en el producto.
Alinear requerimientos con los heads de negocio, asegurando claridad, trazabilidad y acuerdos sobre alcance.
En este rol, buscamos que aportes criterio para equilibrar valor, esfuerzo y riesgo, manteniendo una comunicación fluida entre negocio, tecnología y terceros.

About BJAK The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name. Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you. The Role BJAK is building a Neobank Superapp for Southeast Asia.

As a Technical Product Manager, you’ll own a product vertical end to end—such as payments and expense management, remittance, insurance, or wealth and trading—from strategy, outcomes, and roadmap through to the technical design and delivery of the systems behind it.

This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges. We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal.

The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved. What you'll be doing
Own a vertical end-to-end — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.
Shape the technical design with engineering — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.
Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.
Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.
Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.
Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.
Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation.
What you'll need
Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.
Technical foundation — solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.
Domain — experience in a regulated / high-consequence domain (payments, banking, remittance, insurance, …) or demonstrable fast-ramp ability; understands why money movement is different (correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners you don't control).
AI judgement — hands-on with LLM-based products; can frame a feature as eval-able (offline, online, human feedback); realistic on hallucination/drift/data gaps, including data-blocked vs model-blocked and when a model must not be in the loop at all.
Nice to have — engineer or highly-technical-PM background · zero-to-one · shipped AI-heavy consumer products · defined eval metrics for ML/LLM systems · AI UX + failure-handling intuition · SEA market experience.
Outcomes
Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap
Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch
Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds
AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted
Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged
Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

Location
This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Philippines . We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Philippines . Language English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required. Interview Process Our process is designed to move fast: 1.

Online assessment or practical task 2. Role-specific interview 3. CEO / final round For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized. Originally posted on Himalayas

This is a fully remote position and we're considering candidates in Canada EST. About Product Management: As a Product Manager at Grafana Labs , you'll develop a vision and strategy for your product domain.

You will own your product’s roadmap, collateral, and market research, and you will collaborate with Grafana leadership on fine-tuning your product’s goals. You will be the primary advocate and expert in your area, with a strong ability to communicate needs, functionality, and details effectively both to external customers and internal stakeholders.

The teams and people you will be interacting with will be 100% remote and globally distributed, so strong and proactive communication is essential. Product Managers are the bridge that connect Engineering, Design, and UX to GTM.

You are a facilitator who ensures the free flow of information across these teams and are expected to be technically proficient when representing our products to our customers.

As the Senior Product Manager for Infrastructure Observability (Infra O11y) you’ll be responsible for our most popular Grafana Cloud products that span the infrastructure suite: Kubernetes Monitoring and Cloud Provider Observability. Infra O11y provides our customers with the ability to easily monitor their core services – from our smallest self-serve customers to our largest enterprise customers.
Your primary responsibility will be to help define the vision and ensure the long-term success of Infra O11y, working with your engineering partners to fine-tune product strategy. You will be charting the path forward for net-new product initiatives – like Host Monitoring – balanced with maintaining a strong roadmap and customer satisfaction for our most mature products.
Your role will require heavy customer discovery, understanding user needs, and building consensus and alignment across several Engineering groups and many stakeholders as we look towards simplifying our broader Infra O11y experience for Grafana Cloud. You will also need to flex your GTM muscles and build conviction in areas like competitive analysis and sales enablement to better inform activities like pricing and packaging.
Beyond driving your individual product area, you’ll also need to ensure that the experiences you’re building are tightly woven into our overall Grafana Cloud suite of products, by establishing integration touchpoints with other key offerings like Grafana Cloud Knowledge Graph and Grafana Assistant, so that our customers have a seamless monitoring experience where they can easily navigate between different layers of their architecture through guided explorations and natural language.

Transform ideas and feedback into a product vision and roadmap
Empathize with customer problems in order to collect user needs, requirements, and pain points
Curate and properly represent user feedback to Engineering, while providing evidence to support tradeoffs and priorities
Work closely with PMM to enable GTM on product differentiation, including creating and updating presentations, documentation, website content, datasheets, and whitepapers.
Use your deep product expertise to make decisions about our go-to-market strategies, pricing, packaging, licensing and tiering

Liberis is in the middle of a meaningful shift. We started as a single-product business and are quickly becoming a truly multi-product embedded finance company, with different funding structures, revenue models and customer relationships sitting alongside each other in the same portfolio. That complexity creates real demand for better data, better insight and clearer thinking about how all of it fits together - with this role sitting at the centre of that challange!

As our Senior Data Product Manager, you’ll sit right at the intersection of product, analytics, engineering and senior leadership, helping define the data products that power smarter decisions across Liberis.

You’ll have real ownership over roadmap, prioritisation and ways of working, and your work will directly influence how teams access, understand and use data day to day. This role is a high-impact opportunity for someone who wants to shape how a business uses data at scale!

You’ll be joining a team with a broad remit and a genuine mandate to improve the data experience across the company, so there’s a lot of scope to make the role your own and shape the future of the domain.

You will own the data and insights product for Liberis, building the foundations that let our commercial, credit and operations teams actually understand the business they're running.

That means, thinking carefully about the entities in our data model, how products and customers relate to each other, how those relationships surface in reporting and analysis - and how it eventually all comes out in great dashboards, tools and self-serve capabilities.

This is about shipping products which are genuinely useful, not just technically correct.

Our Engineering Team is going through an AI-first transformation, rethinking how teams are structured and how they ship. Data, insights and analytics are a crucial part of that journey and you will be a key player in leading, innovating and rapidly improving our posture and capabilities at the intersection of data and AI.

If you like solving genuinely hard problems, bringing clarity to complex environments and building products that have visible business impact - this is the role for you!

Your primary job is to help Liberis's commercial decision makers understand the small businesses we serve and how they consider, use and perform across our product range. Doing this well requires a clear conceptual model of the business and a willingness to engage with stakeholders across the business, as well as taste and customer empathy in developing a great insights product including dashboards, insight tools and self-serve capabilities.

You will own the roadmap for our internal data & insight products. Working with stakeholders across commercial, credit, finance and operations, you will define what good looks like and then work with your team to build it. You will run prioritisation, manage the backlog and make decisions about where effort goes.

You will also spend a meaningful amount of time in the detail, reviewing data models and dashboards, asking hard questions about definitions, and making sure what we ship is accurate and trusted.

You will partner closely with the engineering side of your team on how data is modelled and structured in BigQuery and DBT, and with analysts on how it gets presented in Looker. You don't need to write production code, but you need enough technical understanding to be a genuine partner in those conversations. You will also be responsible for continuing to expand our partner-facing reporting, whereby partners gain visibility into their portfolio.

This role requires someone who can think clearly about complex data structures and translate that thinking into products that non-technical people actually find useful. The ideal person has strong conceptual thinking skills, great product instincts and enough technical depth to earn the trust of the engineers and analysts they work with.

· Proven experience in a senior data product or analytics product role in a business with real complexity

· A track record of helping commercial teams make better decisions through better data, not just shipping dashboards

· Strong ability to think about entities, taxonomies and relationships in data

· Hands-on experience with Looker and LookML and familiarity with best practices and scalable approaches to these systems

· Working knowledge of SQL, DBT and BigQuery, enough to engage seriously with how data is modelled and what's feasible, and to express your thinking in code-speak where needed

· Experience working with a multi skilled team of analysts and data engineers

· Clear, confident communication with senior commercial stakeholders

Next steps If this opportunity feels like the right fit for your next career move, we’d love to hear from you!

Even if you don’t meet every requirement, don’t hesitate to apply or reach out to Chess (Internal Recruiter) on

Our hybrid approach

Working together in person helps us move faster, collaborate better, and build a great Liberis culture. Our hybrid working policy requires team members to be in the office at least 3 days a week, but ideally 4 days. At Liberis, we embrace flexibility as a core part of our culture, while also valuing the importance of the time our teams spend together in the office.

Semarchy has grown into an industry leader in the data management space. We're searching for a Product Manager to help expand the Semarchy Data Platform (SDP) and support our development teams. As a Product Manager, you are one of our core creative talents.

Reporting to the Head of Product Management and working closely with engineering, design, and the field, you will turn customer problems and market evidence into product capabilities that customers value — and pay for. Your goal will be to increase the adoption and market fit of the Semarchy Data Platform.

You will own your product scope end-to-end: discovering what customers actually need, framing the problems worth solving, prioritizing ruthlessly, shaping the roadmap, and partnering across teams to bring capabilities to market successfully.

Your early focus is likely to involve Semarchy 's AI-oriented capabilities — such as agentic access to governed Data Products and AI-assisted stewardship — so experience or genuine enthusiasm in this area is a real advantage.

As with any growing product organization, scope and responsibilities will be shaped together and are expected to evolve over time. We are therefore looking for someone adaptable and curious, who thrives when the problem space is still taking shape. Responsibilities
Discovery & customer research: Run structured problem discovery — investigate problem spaces, validate pain intensity and business impact, map current alternatives, and confirm willingness to change. Engage continuously with customers and partners, including active participation in design partner programs.
Focus on customer value: Anchor every decision in customer outcomes rather than mechanisms. Be able to articulate the customer, the problem, and why it matters — and bring that evidence into product decisions.
Roadmapping & prioritization: Own and maintain the roadmap for your area with regular reviews, clear milestones, and transparent change rationale. Prioritize using evidence rather than assumption, make deliberate trade-offs, and contribute to a monthly-updated, prioritized roadmap that reflects what the market actually needs.
Delivery: Partner closely with engineering and design through the full product delivery lifecycle, from discovery to release. Produce specifications and UI concepts, and refine and organize the product backlog — shaping the end-to-end experience, not just features.
Commercialization & field enablement: Play a key role in the commercialization process, coordinating the activities within your scope — such as internal training, previews, enablement, and messaging — so releases reach customers fully field-ready. Contribute captivating documentation and customer-facing assets (blogs, whitepapers, solution briefs) that help the field and marketing communicate value, and participate in commercialization retrospectives.
AI-oriented capabilities (initial focus): Shape how customers connect their enterprise AI ecosystem to governed, trusted data (e.g., agentic / MCP-based access). Explore and validate AI-assisted stewardship and governed AI participation, and help translate fast-moving AI research and prototypes into shippable, differentiated value.
Evangelism: Champion Semarchy products to internal and external audiences — talking to customers, partners, industry analysts, and field personnel — and feed their input back into product strategy and prioritization.

Proven experience as a product manager or product owner in the B2B, SaaS, or technology space, with a solid portfolio.
Demonstrated strength in customer discovery and research — you have talked to many customers and turned what you heard into product decisions.
A clear bias toward value and outcomes — comfortable challenging requests and reframing them around the underlying problem.

Oula delivers maternity care built around our patients—offering comprehensive support before, during, and after pregnancy. With fewer C-sections and higher VBAC success rates, our research-backed approach is delivering better outcomes. Our team of trusted midwives, OBGYNs, and dedicated care navigators ensure our patients get the type of care they need in the moments that matter most.
Since launching in 2021, we’ve expanded to include Preconception and Miscarriage Care, Pregnancy Care, Postpartum Support, and Gynecology. We currently have 4 clinics in the tri-state area, with three new clinics opening in 2026! Come join our team of clinicians, innovators, operators, and technologists passionate about setting a new standard in maternity care.

Product Manager
Full-Time
New York, Chicago or Charlotte

About Oula
Oula Health is a venture-backed, midwifery-led maternity and GYN care company building the next generation of women's healthcare. We partner exclusively with major health systems — including Mount Sinai, Stamford Health, and Novant Health — to embed our collaborative OB-GYN and midwifery model directly inside their networks. We're a team of ~100 people at Series B stage, with 4 clinics today and three more opening in 2026.

At Oula, our product doesn't sit alongside our EHR — it integrates directly into it. Every product and engineering decision has downstream consequences for how our EHRs are configured, and every EHR configuration decision shapes what's possible on the product side. Someone has to hold both at once.
We're looking for a technically-minded Product Manager to own and evolve our core technology stack — including our EHR, patient portal, and care management platform. This role sits at the intersection of product, operations, and health system integration, serving as the internal and external subject matter expert on our EMR and the primary lead for health system EHR integrations.
You'll manage the day-to-day health of our tech stack, partnering closely with both internal teams and external health system stakeholders to ensure our systems run smoothly and our integrations deliver.

You can sit with a midwife and understand why a clinical template matters, then turn around and write a bug ticket that engineering can actually action, then build the SOP so the next market launch doesn't require you to be in the room. When things are ambiguous (and they often are), you'll lean in rather than wait for clarity.
What You'll Own
EHR Configuration & Clinical Systems
Own day-to-day management of our core tech stack: the EHR, patient portal, and care management platform
Own Athena and Epic configuration end to end: clinical templates, order sets, lab configurations, payer connectivity, and access management for clinical and ops staff
Lead EHR integration efforts as the internal and external subject matter expert — FHIR/HL7 data exchange, health system IT coordination and committed go-live timelines
Own and accelerate Epic integration timelines as we onboard additional health system partners
Maintain configuration integrity as new markets launch and care model workflows evolve
Partner with our IT team on infrastructure; own the clinical systems layer they don't touch
Product Operations & Launch
Own bug intake and prioritization from Market Operations — standardize how Engineering receives, scopes, and resolves issues and communicates status back to the field
Build structured launch toolkits and training materials so clinic teams are prepared for new feature rollouts on day one
Coordinate end-to-end launches across Product, Engineering, and Operations
Identify where AI and automation can reduce manual administrative burden in product operations workflows
Standards & Knowledge Management
Build and maintain the clinical systems SOP library so new market setup is repeatable — documented well enough that a new hire can execute without you in the room
Develop onboarding materials for clinic managers and clinical staff on EHR workflows and tooling
Drive feature parity efforts so patients and clinicians experience a consistent standard of care across markets
Data & Reporting
Build and maintain dashboards tracking feature adoption, issue resolution, and rollout health across clinics
Develop quarterly reporting for Product, leadership, and health system partners on platform performance
Ensure data infrastructure is in place to measure the impact of every feature rollout

3+ years with product operations, technical program management, or PM-adjacent work — ideally at a growth-stage digital health or services company
Strong problem-solving instincts and genuine curiosity — you like figuring out how things work and making them work better
Ease with ambiguity and a bias toward action; this role requires you to create the playbook, not execute someone else's
Demonstrated ability to navigate complex stakeholder environments and drive aggressive timelines — ideally with client-facing or health system-facing experience
Ability to speak ‘multiple languages’ – comfort going deep on technical details while communicating clearly to non-technical audiences; you can write a bug ticket, an SOP, and a launch plan that people actually follow; hands-on EHR configuration and integration experience strongly preferred
Analytical enough to build a dashboard and identify a pattern, even if you're not a SQL expert
What Success Looks Like
In your first 90 days, you've audited our current Athena configuration, identified gaps, and have a remediation plan. You understand the bug triage process well enough to have improved it. You've met your counterparts at every health system partner and know what's coming for the next Epic integration.
At six months, new market launches have a repeatable systems and product checklist. Clinic teams know what to expect before a feature goes live. Bug resolution time is measurably faster and the field is no longer sending issues into a black hole.
At one year, the SOP library is comprehensive, clinical systems configuration is stable and documented, and you've successfully navigated at least one new health system EHR environment. The product team has a reliable partner and the ops team isn't dependent on any single person for systems knowledge.

About Faire
Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline.

At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores.

With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.
We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.

We're looking for a Staff Product Manager to treat Faire's data and ML platforms as products: define clear user needs, measurable outcomes, and a roadmap that accelerates every team building on these foundations. You will make data trustworthy by default and make ML capabilities easy to adopt and operate in production. When the data Faire runs on is high-quality and easy to use, every team that depends on it makes better decisions and ships better products.
ML powers Faire's marketplace, from search and recommendations to personalization. Shared data sits underneath nearly every product decision we make, and AI data agents are how that insight shows up in the day-to-day of building product.

This role sits at that foundation: you will run structured discovery with the engineers, scientists, and product teams who build on these platforms, prioritize the investments that unblock them, and hold the bar on quality, reliability, and adoption.

You will also establish the product-platform operating model — roadmap, intake, adoption, measurement — that Faire can extend as the broader product platform function scales.

Own the path from ML idea to production: run structured discovery with ML engineers and data scientists, prioritize platform investments across training, deployment, observability, and model registry, and drive adoption so usage signals shape engineering priorities.
Measure ML platform success through user outcomes, including time saved, models shipped, and support load, rather than process metrics alone.
Scale the use of AI data agents: own the vision for agentic data insights Product, Design, and Engineering use to shape strategy; prioritize the data-engineering investments agents depend on; drive adoption across product development; and measure success through decisions accelerated and time saved on insight work, not demo metrics.
Increase trust in Faire's core data by defining SLAs, driving pipeline health on datasets the business depends on, establishing data contracts and clear dataset ownership, and making the cross-functional case for quality investments that compete with feature work.
Improve metadata quality, lineage, and discovery so teams can find, trust, and trace data, and establish access controls and durable compliance processes for data deletion, access management, and auditability.
Build the data products internal users actually need through embedded discovery: fact and dimension tables, semantic layers, reusable data products, and first-class discoverability and developer experience.
Establish a durable product-platform operating model with a published roadmap the company can plan against, a clear intake process, adoption tracking across usage, retention, and satisfaction, and platform cost and efficiency as a health metric — proven first on data and ML, and built to extend as Faire's product platform function grows.

8+ years of product management experience, with ownership of complex technical products at Staff or Lead scope.
Technical fluency across data and ML platforms: you have worked directly with data and ML systems, can engage credibly with engineering on architecture tradeoffs, understand modern ML in production (model training and deployment, feature pipelines, evaluation), and translate technical complexity into clear strategic choices.
Experience shipping platform products for internal technical users, including discovery, success metrics, adoption, and operational discipline.
Experience shipping in a marketplace or other data-rich product context where the product depends on data feeding algorithmic choices such as search, recommendations, or personalization. You understand how upstream data and ML decisions translate into conversion, relevance, and retention.
Cross-functional influence and strategic prioritization: credibility with senior engineers and data scientists, the ability to negotiate without positional authority, ruthless sequencing, and clarity about what the team is choosing not to do.
Comfort building an operating model, not just a roadmap: you have established discovery, intake, and measurement practices that other teams could adopt, and you are energized by growing a platform practice beyond its initial domain.

Truecaller's ads business reaches over 400 million users and is one of the largest in-app advertising platforms in its markets.

We are building a modern, server-driven programmatic stack that we own end to end, and this role owns the platform at the heart of it: the intelligence layer that powers demand-supply matching across all our demand channels.

Every ad opportunity flows through this platform, and it decides how that opportunity is valued, priced, auctioned, and allocated to maximize revenue while protecting user experience.
This is a senior, high-ownership role at the center of a multi-year platform build, working closely with engineering, data science, and the supply and demand product teams.

Own the platform strategy and roadmap: the decisioning, auction, and pricing systems that sit between our supply and our demand partners.
Build auction intelligence: bid landscape analysis, pricing and floor strategies, auction design, and demand orchestration that decides which demand sources to invoke for each opportunity.
Drive yield: deliver measurable improvements in eCPM, fill, win rate, and incremental revenue; identify revenue leakage and close it through platform enhancements.
Optimize for scale: drive initiatives around platform performance, reliability, and latency as traffic volumes and demand partners grow.
Shape the long-term architecture: capabilities like traffic shaping, audience-based packaging, and curated marketplaces that turn the platform into a durable competitive advantage.
Run a rigorous operating cadence: define platform KPIs and operational health metrics, design controlled experiments, and iterate based on measured impact.

6+ years in product management, with 3+ years in ad tech, programmatic advertising, or publisher monetization platforms. Hands-on experience driving revenue growth through programmatic is essential.
Programmatic depth: Strong understanding of the ecosystem, including unified auctions, header bidding, open bidding, mediation models, oRTB, and auction dynamics. Working knowledge of platforms such as Google Ad Manager, PubMatic, or ironSource.
Monetization fluency: comfort with the full KPI stack (eCPM, fill rate, match rate, win rate, bid density, viewability, ARPU) and a track record of using it to find and capture yield.
Platform product skills: proven experience building large-scale platform products with engineering-heavy teams, and the ability to translate complex business problems into scalable platform capabilities. Good understanding of distributed systems, APIs, and latency-sensitive architecture.
Data-driven rigor: strong analytical skills, comfort with large datasets, and fluency in experimentation, A/B testing, and controlled rollouts.
Stakeholder influence: ability to align engineering, data science, ad operations, and sales around a common platform strategy using data and business insight.

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.
We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.
AI agents are changing how everyone works — not just developers writing code, but entire organizations building, deploying, and operating software. Agents are becoming teammates: they write code, run tests, manage infrastructure, analyze data, and automate workflows across every function.

Docker is building a new platform from scratch to make this real — secure execution environments, agent-to-tool connectivity, governance controls, and the infrastructure that lets agents and humans collaborate safely at enterprise scale.
This is a 0-to-1 role. You will define the product strategy and own the roadmap for a new platform that sits at the intersection of AI, containers, and developer experience. You will work with a small, high-velocity team spanning engineering, design, and go-to-market to figure out what to build, ship it, learn from it, and iterate. The early signal is already in market — Docker Sandboxes is one of the fastest-growing new products in Docker’s history — and the opportunity ahead is much larger.
We are looking for someone who builds, not just plans. You should be comfortable prototyping, getting your hands dirty with early product iterations, and improvising when things don’t go as expected. The right candidate has shipped developer tools or infrastructure products, understands how the agentic AI ecosystem is evolving, and thrives in the ambiguity of building something genuinely new.

Own the product strategy. Define the vision, roadmap, and success metrics for Docker’s AI & Agent Platform. Make hard tradeoff decisions about what to build, what to defer, and what to cut.
Build from zero. This is a new platform. You will define the product from the ground up — writing the first specs, prototyping with engineering, validating with customers, and iterating rapidly based on what you learn.
Drive from conception through delivery. Write requirements, work with engineering to scope and prioritize, ship iteratively, and measure outcomes. You don’t hand off specs and wait — you are in the details.
Define how pieces of the agentic ecosystem fit together. Agents need secure execution, tool connectivity, model access, governance, and observability. You will define how these capabilities compose into a coherent platform — and where Docker’s boundaries are.
Think beyond developers. Agents are becoming essential for everyone who builds, deploys, and operates software. You will ensure the platform serves the full range of people who need agents to succeed — from individual developers to platform teams to enterprise operators.
Define the developer experience. Work with design and engineering to ensure that our AI products are intuitive, powerful, and meet people where they are — whether in the CLI, IDE, or CI pipeline.
Collaborate across Docker. You will work cross-functionally to ensure coherent product experiences and go-to-market alignment.
Influence technical direction. Partner with engineering leadership on architecture decisions. You don’t need to write the code, but you need to understand the technical tradeoffs and have informed opinions about them.
Represent the customer. Engage directly with developers, enterprises, and partners. Bring their voice into every product decision.
Overcome blockers. When something is in the way — a missing integration, an unclear market signal, a technical constraint — you figure out a path forward. You don’t wait for someone else to solve the problem.

Experience . 10+ years of product management experience, with at least 5 years on developer tools, infrastructure, or platform products.
Deep technical fluency. You can read an architecture diagram, understand container and VM runtimes, and have a working knowledge of how AI agents, LLMs, and protocol-level tool connectivity work. You don’t need to be a hypervisor engineer, but you need to hold your own with one.
Proven ability to ship 0-to-1 products. You have taken a product from idea through launch in a fast-moving environment. You know how to operate when there is no playbook.
Builder mentality. You prototype, you sketch architectures, you test early ideas with customers before the spec is done. You are a doer, not just a thinker.
Strong product sense and UX instincts. You care about the developer experience at a deep level — from API design to CLI ergonomics to error messages.
Strategic thinking with execution follow-through. You can set a multi-year vision and also write the spec for what ships next sprint.
Comfort with ambiguity. This space is new and moving fast. You thrive when the answer isn’t obvious and you have to go find it.
Excellent communication. You can write a crisp product brief, present to executives, and debate technical tradeoffs with engineers — all in the same day.
Experience growing and monetizing products at scale. You have been part of taking a product from early adoption to meaningful revenue, and you understand the pricing, packaging, and go-to-market decisions that make that happen.

Experience building products in the containers, cloud-native, or DevOps space
Experience with AI/ML developer tooling or the agentic AI ecosystem
Contributions to open source projects
Experience building and scaling a business from zero to significant ARR
What You’ll Work With
We are building a new platform for agentic development. Docker Sandboxes — isolated execution environments for AI coding agents — is one of the first products in this platform and one of the fastest-growing new products in Docker’s history. But this is just the beginning. The platform will grow to span multiple product areas as we define how agents and people work together at scale.

s.h: The technologies you will work across include
s.t:
Secure, isolated execution environments (microVMs, containers, sandboxing)
Agent-to-tool connectivity and protocol standards (MCP and beyond)
AI model serving and inference infrastructure
Governance, policy enforcement, and audit controls for enterprise AI adoption
Local-to-cloud execution and workload portability
Developer CLIs, SDKs, and platform APIs
Container runtimes, image registries, and build systems

We are building the world's decision infrastructure: the strategic twin of every industrial organization for complex combinatorial problems. We unlocked what wasn't possible before: mapping reality with its levers and constraints into a computer, then running n-dimensional optimization on critical value-chain decisions. We help Europe stay strong and the German Mittelstand make good decisions between market shifts, orders, machines and people.
Founded by Dana (CEO) and Erik (CTO) from RWTH research, backed by a €2.8M round led by Vorwerk Ventures, with customers live on our optimization models.
We move fast. We care. No patience for problems left unsolved.

You own the product and the priorities behind it. The hard part of that job here is structural: our go-to-market runs vertically, one use case at a time, while the product has to stay general enough to serve the next customer without being rebuilt.
You sit between Sales and Engineering and translate in both directions. Towards Sales: which use cases we can sell today, which we cannot, and what a demo is allowed to claim. Towards Engineering: which requirement is ready to be built, what it needs to be complete, and what we deliberately leave out.
This is an early-stage role and we expect you to shape it rather than inherit it. We are extending the core of the application right now, which means your first decisions land while the product is still taking form. At the beginning, a meaningful part of your work will be spent on customer projects, close to the people whose decisions we model. That is where you see which patterns are worth turning into product.
We will not sugarcoat it: short deadlines, wild workload, and a go to market with the product and its tech that is a day to day focus and iteration process.
What you'll own
The product roadmap and the reasoning behind it: what we build next, in which order, and what we decline.
The boundary between standard product, configuration, and manual work for one customer.
Requirements that engineering can build from: scope, acceptance criteria, and a clear statement of what is out.
What we can credibly promise a customer, including where the product's limits currently are.
Proofs of Value that you run yourself, and responsibility for individual accounts.
Prototypes you build to test features with customers before we commit engineering time.
How product works here: discovery, prioritisation, and the standards between product and engineering.
Your number: how much of what is project work today is standard product a year from now, and the time from a recognised customer problem to a usable capability.
This role is not for you if your strength is backlog, process and ceremonies, if you need research and design capacity before you can decide, if a complex industrial domain is an obstacle rather than the interesting part, if you don't like data or if you need more than three days before your first customer conversation.

s.t:
Experience: 15+ years of product management experience, including owning and driving large-scale technology platforms, AI products, developer-facing products, or enterprise SaaS capabilities across multiple lifecycle stages.

Agentic AI Product Thinking: Strong understanding of how AI, LLMs, agents, tools, workflows, automation, and orchestration can be applied to enterprise SaaS products. Ability to think beyond chatbot experiences and define how AI can help users complete meaningful tasks and business outcomes.

AI Quality and Governance: Familiarity with AI evaluation methods such as golden datasets, test suites, trace analysis, human review, LLM-as-a-judge, regression testing, and production monitoring. Strong awareness of AI risks around accuracy, privacy, security, explainability, permissions, and compliance.

Technical Depth: Deep familiarity with cloud platforms, SaaS business models, microservices, serverless computing, event-driven architectures, API-first design, data integrations, and modern enterprise architecture. Ability to translate technical possibilities into product outcomes.

Platform Product Management: Strong platform mindset with experience creating reusable capabilities, standards, interfaces, and services that support multiple product teams and business use cases.
